Optionality / Constraint: Each activity must resolve to exactly one user.
Example Business Rule: A user can attempt many tasks; an activity cannot belong to multiple users.

Optionality / Constraint: Every reward ledger entry belongs to one user.
Example Business Rule: A user can receive multiple reward entries, including adjustments.

Optionality / Constraint: A reward may reference one originating activity; some reward types may have no task source.
Example Business Rule: One completed activity may generate more than one reward component only if the reward policy permits it.

Optionality / Constraint: Every wallet ledger row belongs to one user.
Example Business Rule: Wallet balance is derived from posted ledger entries, not a mutable analytics-only balance.

Optionality / Constraint: A reward may post to one or more wallet rows depending on ledger design; document one-to-one if that is the actual contract.
Example Business Rule: Do not assume reward amount equals wallet movement without a transaction link.

Optionality / Constraint: Every withdrawal request belongs to one user.
Example Business Rule: A user may submit multiple withdrawal requests over time.
Use a bridge or explicit withdrawal_id on ledger rows if multiple movements can settle one withdrawal.

Cardinality: 1 to many as referrer; 1 to many as referee
Optionality / Constraint: Both user references must be valid and roles must not be conflated.
Example Business Rule: A referral is one referral relationship record linking inviter and invitee.

Optionality / Constraint: System events without a user must allow nullable user_id only with a documented actor/system identity.
Example Business Rule: Do not drop anonymous/system events solely because user_id is absent.

Optionality / Constraint: Ticket may be user-linked; system-generated tickets need explicit source identity.
Example Business Rule: One user may raise many support tickets.

Cardinality: 1 to many (optional) / many-to-many if content reused across events
Foreign Key / Bridge: Feature Events.content_id; bridge if multiple content objects per event
Optionality / Constraint: Use a bridge table if one event references multiple content assets.
Example Business Rule: Keep content view and content completion distinct.

Optionality / Constraint: One activity can receive multiple provider callbacks/retries; callback identity must be unique.
Example Business Rule: Retain raw callbacks and canonical mapped state separately.
